issue.title: Short-circuit in a mapped task group lets later all_done and none_failed tasks run
issue.body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version

main (as of 2026-10-03); also reproduced on 3.1.8

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

Inside a mapped task group, a short-circuit task that returns False skips only the task right after it. Later tasks of the same map index still run if their trigger rule accepts a skipped upstream (`all_done`, `none_failed`), even with the default `ignore_downstream_trigger_rules=True`.

```python
import pendulum

from airflow.sdk import dag, task, task_group


@dag(schedule=None, start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 1, 1, tz="UTC"), catchup=False)
def short_circuit_mapped_group():
    @task_group
    def group(value):
        @task.short_circuit  # ignore_downstream_trigger_rules=True (default)
        def gate(v):
            return v

        @task
        def a():
            pass

        @task(trigger_rule="all_done")  # "none_failed" behaves the same
        def b():
            pass

        gate(value) >> a() >> b()

    group.expand(value=[True, False])


short_circuit_mapped_group()
```

Steps: run `airflow standalone` (SQLite, LocalExecutor), trigger the Dag and check the task instances of map index 1. `airflow dags test short_circuit_mapped_group` gives the same states.

Map index 1 (`gate` returns False):

| Build | `group.a[1]` | `group.b[1]`, `all_done` | `group.b[1]`, `none_failed` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1.8 | skipped | success | success |
| main | skipped | success | success |

Map index 0 runs everything, as expected. Controls on the same builds:

- The same chain outside a mapped task group: `a` and `b` are skipped.
- `ignore_downstream_trigger_rules=False` in the mapped group: `b[1]` runs, the same as with `True`.
- `b` with the default `all_success`: `b[1]` is skipped, because the skip propagates through `a`.

### What you think should happen instead?

`group.b[1]` should be skipped. The ShortCircuitOperator docs say that with `ignore_downstream_trigger_rules=True`, "all downstream tasks are skipped without considering the `trigger_rule` defined for tasks". That holds outside a mapped task group, but inside one the flag currently has no effect.

The XCom that `gate` writes for map index 1 lists both `group.a` and `group.b`. For a mapped task instance, `SkipMixin._set_state_to_skipped` in `task-sdk/src/airflow/sdk/bases/skipmixin.py` does not skip anything itself and leaves it to `NotPreviouslySkippedDep`, which only reads the decision of direct upstream tasks, so only `group.a` picks it up.

### Operating System

macOS 26.2

### Deployment

Virtualenv installation

### Apache Airflow Provider(s)

standard

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers

apache-airflow-providers-standard 1.12.0 (with 3.1.8); main installed from source.

### Official Helm Chart version

Not Applicable

### Kubernetes Version

Not Applicable

### Helm Chart configuration

Not Applicable

### Docker Image customizations

Not Applicable

### Anything else?

It happens every time. The main build I tested already includes #73959 and #73960, the two fixes from #55225; this case is not covered by either. On 3.2.0 to 3.3.2, nothing inside a mapped task group is skipped at all, not even `group.a[1]`, which #73959 fixed on main. #73960 covers a different case: an unmapped short-circuit with an expanded mapped downstream task.

comments.body: Hey @luc-pimentel, I would like to work on this can you assign this to me

> Hey [@luc-pimentel](https://github.com/luc-pimentel), I would like to work on this can you assign this to me

Currently we don't assign contributors to issues according to policy (with some exceptions).
Feel free to create a PR without assignment.

I’ve reproduced the issue and identified the cause in `NotPreviouslySkippedDep`.

The fix updates it to consider all upstream relatives so that skip decisions from a `ShortCircuitOperator` inside a mapped task group are correctly respected by transitive downstream tasks.

I’ve also added a regression test and verified that the reported behavior is fixed.

A PR is being opened with the fix: `Fix mapped task group short circuit skipping`.

If this approach needs any changes or there’s a better way to address the issue, I’m happy to discuss and adjust the implementation.
